title: Multi-agent coordination: scoped specialists and shared evidence
objectives: Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects multi-agent coordination: scoped specialists and shared evidence with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. For failure triage, compare a log specialist and history specialist against one bounded assistant.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: Multiple agents are useful when specialties or independently verifiable subtasks justify coordination overhead. A supervisor routes work and integrates results; specialists operate within narrower tools and evidence scopes. Handoffs transfer a typed task, relevant evidence and a remaining budget, not an unrestricted conversation dump.
More agents can amplify latency, cost, inconsistent conclusions and failure propagation. Compare the design against a single-agent or deterministic baseline before adding roles.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Use task IDs, parent IDs, owner, status, evidence IDs and result schemas. Independent read-only analyses can run in parallel; writes and dependent analyses require ordered coordination. The supervisor merges evidence by stable ID and checks contradictions before making a recommendation.

Allocate a shared total budget rather than giving each specialist a fresh unlimited budget. A specialist failure returns an explicit error or uncertainty; the supervisor must not convert missing work into fabricated success.
sections.code:
results=[{'task':'logs','evidence':['F1']},{'task':'history','evidence':['F1','F2']}]
merged=sorted({e for r in results for e in r['evidence']})
assert merged==['F1','F2']

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: Two agents edit the same file concurrently, and the supervisor accepts the last result without conflict review. Another agent recursively delegates until the call count explodes. Shared memory containing another tenant's records creates an additional security boundary.

Test conflicting recommendations, duplicated evidence, failed handoffs, cancellation propagation and shared-budget exhaustion. Use deterministic specialist fixtures to validate orchestration independently from reasoning quality.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: For failure triage, compare a log specialist and history specialist against one bounded assistant. Measure independent evidence gain, completion rate, latency and coordination calls. Keep the simpler design if the extra agents add no useful evidence.
An SDET report should expose each task's input scope and output provenance. Final correctness cannot conceal an unauthorized specialist action or an unresolved conflicting conclusion.

takeaway: For failure triage, compare a log specialist and history specialist against one bounded assistant.

title: Coordinate specialist budgets and merge conflicts
objectives: Coordinate specialist budgets and merge conflicts
Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects coordinate specialist budgets and merge conflicts with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. Release evidence includes task scopes, allocations, actual usage and integrated conclusions.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: Parallel specialists can inspect independent evidence, but they share one user task and one resource budget. Giving each specialist the full budget multiplies the possible total cost. Shared state needs an explicit merge policy and evidence provenance; last-writer-wins can hide a conflicting conclusion.

The supervisor should integrate findings rather than merely concatenate answers. If a log specialist identifies automation timing while a history specialist suggests a product regression, preserve the disagreement and identify the additional evidence needed.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Assign task IDs, scoped inputs, per-task ceilings and a shared remaining allowance. Reserve budget before delegation and settle actual usage afterward. Keep results as typed records with evidence IDs, status and uncertainty. Deduplicate source IDs without discarding which specialist used them.

Independent reads can run concurrently; dependent analysis and side effects remain ordered. A failed child task returns an explicit failed result, and cancellation propagates to all pending work. The parent cannot mark missing results successful.

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: Two specialists each spend eight calls against a ten-call parent limit. Another specialist writes a conclusion into shared state while a second overwrites it without conflict review. These failures may be invisible in the final prose.

Test budget reservation, duplicate task IDs, late results after cancellation and conflicting evidence. Compare total steps and latency against a single-agent baseline before retaining the more complex design.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: Release evidence includes task scopes, allocations, actual usage and integrated conclusions. Measure whether specialization improves task completion or evidence coverage enough to justify coordination cost.

For SDETs, orchestration tests should use deterministic specialist results first. This isolates coordination correctness from model behavior and makes race conditions and failure propagation reproducible.

mistake: Two specialists each spend eight calls against a ten-call parent limit. Another specialist writes a conclusion into shared state while a second overwrites it without conflict review. These failures may be invisible in the final prose.
takeaway: Release evidence includes task scopes, allocations, actual usage and integrated conclusions.
